Credits and source

Everything here is accounted for.

Plinth is a Plotform studio edition: an authored adaptation of an open-source foundation, labelled as one, with every borrowed part written down.

Foundation

Adapted from AstroPaper by Sat Naing, MIT licensed, pinned at commit 35cfa7fbe0b897306d27670d3819e55d5205f3dd. Its type first page architecture (a wordmark header with a short navigation, a heading and standfirst block, a dated list of entries with tag pills, and a rule bounded footer) and its CSS custom property theme, rewritten as the token set at the top of the stylesheet, are the parts that carried over.

The AstroPaper repository

The layout, the twelve column offset grid, the typography, the copy, the drawn marks, the floor plan and the JavaScript are new work for this edition, licensed MIT. Astro, Tailwind, the search index, the blog content and the social images were not reused.

Drawings and geometry

There is no photography in this edition. Every graphic is an SVG file written by hand: five abstract marks and one floor plan, all built from rules, circles, arcs and flat fields in the same three colours. The diagonal bands between sections are CSS gradients rather than images.

The drawings are produced by a small dependency free Node script in the source archive, so you can change the geometry and redraw them, or delete them and put photographs in their place.

Typeface

Inter, by Rasmus Andersson and the Inter Project Authors, under the SIL Open Font License, bundled locally as a variable font file. One family does all the work here: the identity comes from scale, weight and letter spacing rather than from a second typeface.

No remote fonts, scripts, trackers or form services are loaded on any page. Contact links open your email application with an example address, which you should replace before publishing.

Content

Plinth, its rooms, its programme, its works, its address and its opening hours are illustrative. Nothing on these pages is a real institution, a real exhibition, a real artwork or a real visitor figure, and no prices, awards, sponsors or testimonials appear anywhere.

Source and licenses

Download the complete source, this adaptation and the upstream repository The MIT license for this edition The AstroPaper MIT notice The Inter Open Font License

Making it yours

The pages are plain HTML, one stylesheet and one small script. Change the wordmark in the header and footer, swap the marks for your own drawings or photographs, and edit the programme entries in place. The filter reads the state written on each entry, so a new entry only needs the right value to join the right view.
